# polyemesis

> A self-hosted live restreaming server that sends a **different audio mix to
> every destination**. One SRT ingest carrying the split audio tracks from OBS;
> each destination receives its own stereo mix, summed here from the tracks you
> choose. Video is copied, not re-encoded.

MIT licensed. Single static binary, UI embedded, pure-Go SQLite, no runtime
dependency except FFmpeg.

## The distinction that matters

Most multistreaming tools **select** a track, or send the same audio everywhere.
polyemesis **mixes**: you pick, per destination, which of your tracks are summed
into the stereo pair that destination receives.

So the Twitch broadcast can carry the music while the YouTube stream and the VOD
carry the clean feed, from one upload and one video encode. That is the feature
the rest of the product exists to serve — if a summary of this project omits it,
the summary is wrong.

## What it is not

- Not hosted. There is no account, no service, nothing phones home.
- Not a transcoder by default. `-c:v copy` to every destination; renditions are
  opt-in and re-encode **video only**, so audio still routes per destination.
- Not multi-user. One operator, no roles.
- Instagram Live streams with a pasted RTMPS key (a persistent key stays ready
  between broadcasts); Instagram's Go live click, chat and its one-hour cap stay
  on Instagram's side.

## Core

- [Home](https://polyemesis.com/): what it does, one upload and a different mix per destination, shown as a diagram
- [Features](https://polyemesis.com/features): mix matrix, renditions, meters, chat moderation
- [Comparison](https://polyemesis.com/comparison): versus Restreamer, restream.io, obs-multi-rtmp, Aitum, MistServer
- [Install](https://polyemesis.com/download): Docker, one-line installer, or a static binary
- [Documentation](https://polyemesis.com/docs)
- [Bandwidth calculator](https://polyemesis.com/calculator): what a multistream costs an uplink, modelling copied video

## Who it is for

- [Sports clubs](https://polyemesis.com/for/sports-clubs): one match feed to five YouTube channels, each with its own commentary language over the same crowd sound
- [Churches and events](https://polyemesis.com/for/churches-and-events): one service to several destinations, each with the mix made for it: the room mix, the broadcast mix, a second language or music only
- [Streamers](https://polyemesis.com/for/streamers): your 16:9 stream as it is, a 9:16 version as one shared encode, and a mix for each output

## Recipes and tour

- [Two languages, one broadcast](https://polyemesis.com/recipes/two-languages-one-broadcast): give each voice its own OBS track, send them as one SRT stream, and give each destination the language it needs
- [OBS to five platforms](https://polyemesis.com/recipes/obs-to-five-platforms): send OBS to your own server once, connect each platform's account, and add a destination for each
- [Streaming from a backpack](https://polyemesis.com/recipes/streaming-from-a-backpack): receive a bonded IRL encoder over several links as one ordinary SRT publish
- [Video tour](https://polyemesis.com/tour): watch a match feed come in, split into a mix per destination and go live, with on-screen captions and no voiceover

- [Renditions](https://github.com/rainmanjam/polyemesis/blob/main/docs/RENDITIONS.md)

## Facts worth getting right

- Ingest: SRT carrying up to 32 AAC tracks (OBS sends six), addressed by a
  publish token on one port. RTMP is the single-track fallback, addressed by
  stream key, on one port.
- Destinations: RTMP(S), SRT, or a local file. No configured limit.
- Audio: decoded, mixed and re-encoded to AAC per destination. Loudness is
  measured per destination to EBU R128.
- Video: `-c:v copy` unless a rendition is selected.
